transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Emma Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Anya Kuznetsov (Redwood SE), James Holloway (CTO, KeystonePay), Rina Singh (Head of ML), Vikram Das (Infra Lead), Sophie Park (PM)

Summary:
KeystonePay is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a reserved GPU deployment to serve real-time fraud-detection and conversational agent workloads. Primary concerns: isolation/data residency, predictable throughput for peak windows, burst-to-hosted capability for spikes, autoscaling behavior, and compliance (SOC2/KMS/SSO). They requested pricing tiers for committed capacity, an architecture diagram for VPC/private deployment, and a benchmarking run with their sample traffic.

Topics:
- Current stack and traffic patterns
- Throughput & latency SLOs
- Dedicated capacity sizing and burst strategies
- Networking/VPC and private deployment concerns
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO)
- Next steps and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Emma: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Emma from Redwood, AE on this account, with Carlos and Anya from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] James: Good, thanks. We kicked off a quick discovery doc but wanted to hear how Redwood thinks about dedicated capacity for, ya know, real production inference.
[00:17] Emma: Great. Can you start with a quick high-level of your workloads and traffic?
[00:22] Rina: Sure - Rina here. Two primary workloads: a token classification model for fraud scoring that runs on transaction payloads (low-latency scoring, ~200 qps baseline, 800 qps peaks for 10-15 minutes during rollouts) and a conversational routing agent that serves customer support flows (batches and streaming responses).
[00:40] Vikram: Our infra is mostly GCP, VPC peered to partner networks. We need isolated hardware for PCI-adjacent data and cannot send raw PII outside our VPC.
[00:49] Carlos: Thanks. So sounds like dedicated makes sense for isolation. A couple clarifying Qs: what model sizes are you serving and typical sequence lengths?
[00:58] Rina: Fraud model's pretty lean - 7B quantized. Conversational agent is a fine-tuned 34B, around 1k token context for some cases. Latency target for fraud scoring is sub-150ms p95 if possible.
[01:12] Emma: Great. On dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools, you can pin model versions and we support private deployments (VPC) so the model and inference path can stay in your network. The dedicated pools are configured by GPU class; we have options for A10/A100 equivalents depending on throughput/latency needs.
[01:30] James: Curious about bursting: we don't want to pay for peak 24/7. Can you explain burst-to-hosted?
[01:36] Carlos: Yeah, so the pattern we recommend is a committed baseline for steady qps and an allowed burst window where additional requests overflow to Redwood Hosted capacity. We can configure routing policies so sensitive workloads don't leave the private network — so for PCI-sensitive calls you may choose no-burst. There's nuance: bursting to hosted means data plane leaves your dedicated pool, so for strict isolation you'd keep everything on Dedicated.
[01:58] Vikram: Right, we probably need the fraud model to stay strictly in our VPC. Conversational stuff may be okay to burst.
[02:06] Anya: Another lever is autoscaling on the dedicated pool. We can recommend scaling policies (scale by tokens/sec or GPU utilization). For your 800 qps spikes, we typically suggest a small headroom (20-30%) and a quick scale-up strategy with warm standby instances to reduce cold-starts.
[02:24] Rina: Warm standby — so those GPUs are reserved but not fully utilized? Cost implications?
[02:29] Carlos: Correct. Warm standby is effectively reserved but lower-cost because you're not paying for extra ephemeral burst on hosted, but you are committing capacity. We'll include pricing comparisons in the follow-up.
[02:38] James: What about latency variability during the bursts or scale events? We need p95 to stay under 150ms for fraud.
[02:45] Carlos: If you keep fraud on Dedicated and size the pool for peak or use warm standbys, you can maintain p95. If you choose to overflow to Hosted during bursts, latency may be slightly higher depending on region and model variant; we also support routing to lower-latency model variants if availability is constrained.
[03:03] Vikram: How do you handle KV cache and batching? Our fraud model benefits from small batch sizes and prefix caching.
[03:10] Anya: We have KV cache management and continuous batching; caching helps reduce per-token latency for repeated contexts. Batching is workload-aware — your fraud scoring likely stays small batches. We'll capture these details for the benchmark plan.
[03:22] Sophie: On security, we need to see KMS/HSM support, audit logs, and SSO integration. SOC 2 is a must.
[03:29] Emma: Totally. We'll attach our SOC 2 report and a security pack. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, SAML SSO, RBAC, and an audit log stream. Note sometimes the transcript says KMS as K-M-S or K-M-S-H but the meaning is the same.
[03:45] James: Network-wise, how does peering work? Can you do private link or do you require VPN?
[03:51] Carlos: We support VPC peering and private connectivity options; for on-prem we offer direct connect/partner links. We'll include a network diagram in the follow-up.
[03:59] Rina: For the conversational model we care about model variants and quantization — can Redwood run quantized 34B reliably with our latency goals?
[04:07] Anya: Yes, we recommend quantization for 34B in dedicated for cost efficiency. The runtime selects optimized kernels and can maintain throughput; we'll show benchmark numbers for 34B int8/4-bit runs. There may be small accuracy differences; that's why we recommend evals tied to your prompt set.
[04:26] James: Licensing/commitments — what's the minimum commit? And are there options for burst credits?
[04:33] Emma: We have monthly and annual reserved capacity contracts. Minimum depends on GPU class and region; typical enterprise pilots start with a 3-6 month commit. We also offer burst credits that let you overflow to Hosted at reduced rates for a limited window. We'll include exact tiers in the pricing doc.
[04:52] Vikram: SLA — what uptime and latency guarantees for Dedicated?
[04:56] Carlos: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime targets (we'll include the SLA doc). Latency SLOs depend on model and sizing; we provide latency baselines for common model classes. For strict p95 goals we recommend sizing for peak or using warm standby to avoid scale lag.
[05:12] Rina: Any regulatory constraints around logs and data residency? We need log retention controls and options to keep logs in our account.
[05:18] Emma: Yes, we can push audit logs to your logging bucket, and retention/purge policies are configurable. For Private/on-prem, logs never leave your environment unless you configure otherwise.
[05:28] James: Great. What's the typical timeline for onboarding to Dedicated?
[05:32] Carlos: From signed contract to initial deployment usually 4-8 weeks depending on region and networking setup. Pilot benchmark can start in 1-2 weeks if you provide sample workloads and credentials for peering.
[05:44] Sophie: Ok - stakeholders for next steps: James (exec), Rina (ML), Vikram (Infra), Sophie (PM).
[05:51] Emma: Perfect. We'll send the pricing and security pack and propose 2 benchmark slots next week. Any other questions?
[05:58] Rina: One quick thing — we want a clear rollback/fallback plan if Dedicated has issues. Do you support automatic failover to hosted model variants?
[06:06] Anya: Yes — routing policies can be configured to fail over to a hosted-compatible model variant, or to a reduced feature set. This is customizable per route. We'll include an example policy.
[06:17] James: Also curious about cost-per-token estimates for quantized 34B on Dedicated vs Hosted.
[06:22] Carlos: We'll include modeled unit economics with options: baseline reserved capacity cost amortized over expected qps, quantization savings, and burst pricing.
[06:30] Emma: To recap, action items: Emma will email pricing and commitment options; Carlos will prepare a benchmark plan; Vikram will send infra diagram; Redwood will share SOC2 and security pack; and we'll schedule benchmarking run.
[06:44] James: Sounds good. Let's aim to review pricing by Fri.
[06:48] Emma: I'll get that out by Friday. Thanks, everyone.

(Transcript includes a few minor transcription artifacts — e.g., some product names transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "KV cash" — original meanings clarified in notes.)

End of call.
